💡 Key Takeaways
  • 10 stocks we like better than Vanguard Energy ETF ›.
  • Elections have a way of eliciting emotional, borderline-visceral reactions in the investment community.
  • It has been revealed that for those in the camp of doing nothing with their portfolios following the blue wave, there's nothing wrong with that line of thinking.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Todd Shriber – Nov 21, 2026 at 10:30PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Vanguard Energy ETF ›.

Elections have a way of eliciting emotional, borderline-visceral reactions in the investment community. Still, the knee-jerk responses are often confined to the immediate aftermath and, over time, cooler heads ultimately prevail.

It has been revealed that for those in the camp of doing nothing with their portfolios following the blue wave, there's nothing wrong with that line of thinking. That's a calm, rational approach, and one that is validated by history.

Sources indicate that since 1950, the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) has been positive in the year following every midterm election, with an average gain of 15% over those 12 months. So if history holds up, now isn't the time to sell stocks.

Recent findings suggest that investors don’t need to do a lot post-election portfolio tinkering, but these ETFs may be worth examining. Image source: Getty Images.

Sources indicate that on the other hand, changes in congressional majorities may usher in opportunities for tactical investors to capitalize on the latest legislative landscape. Likewise (and perhaps surprisingly), some sectors and industries previously considered vulnerable to the Democratic sweep may prove to be less so. With that in mind, here are some exchange-traded funds (ETFs) I'm spying following the election.

According to recent reports, it's not surprising that the healthcare sector is in the spotlight following Election Day, but this is an example of investors needing to be tactical. Said another way, a standard pharmaceutical-heavy ETF may not be the best way to capitalize on the shift of power in Congress. That's why I'm evaluating the iShares U.S. Healthcare Providers ETF (IHF +0.74%).

According to recent reports, this $1.6 billion ETF, which turned 20 years old in May, holds shares of health insurance providers and service operators. Those could be some of the best healthcare stocks to own at a time when Democrats could push to restore, even in part, the Affordable Care Act's enhanced premium subsidies that fell by the wayside at the end of 2025. There's also chatter about momentum to add long-term care coverage to Medicare, which could benefit some of this ETF's 61 holdings.

NYSEMKT · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

It has been revealed that the new congressional majority could also scrap or significantly limit planned cuts to Medicaid. If Democrats are successful in leveraging government funding to increase insurance coverage, some of this ETF's holdings will benefit from higher enrollment and reduced exposure to uncompensated care.

Be advised that this ETF is top-heavy, as UnitedHealth and CVS Health combine for nearly a third of its portfolio.

The Vanguard Energy ETF (VDE -0.73%) and the Vanguard Information Technology ETF (VGT -7.00%) are both examples of sector ETFs that were decked following Election Day. Since Nov. 4, the first trading day after Election Day, the energy fund dipped 5.3% while its tech counterpart slumped 15.3%.

The reasons differ. As has been widely noted, data center stocks are retreating not only because Democrats will control Congress but also because the party holds 30 of 50 governors' mansions, including some in states where data centers were front and center on Election Day.

In a recent development, clearly, rhetoric opposed to data centers is effective on the campaign trail. Still, the Vanguard tech ETF may not be worth dumping today because it's hard to get data center moratoriums across the legislative finish line. Before Election Day, only Latest York state was successful in climbing that mountain.

NYSEMKT · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

According to recent reports, as for the Vanguard Energy ETF, its post-election weakness isn't surprising. Renewable energy stocks often rally when polls and election results favor Democrats while the fossil fuel names that dominate this Vanguard ETF languish. That scenario played out this year.

Don't rush to abandon or ignore this Vanguard fund. The reasoning is simple: The energy sector has noteworthy short-term earnings momentum, and the group is proving to be an effective portfolio hedge while high interest rates diminish the diversification benefits of bonds.

On that note, it should be acknowledged that energy stocks have been negatively correlated with the broader market for much of this year, implying that the Vanguard Energy ETF can enhance a portfolio’s diversification.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Robert Izquierdo – Nov 21, 2026 at 10:39PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Cava Group ›.

CAVA Group (CAVA -4.67%) runs Mediterranean fasts-casual restaurants and sells food to grocery stores. It operates 500 locations, and opened its first Wisconsin restaurant, located in the city of Greenfield, on Oct. 28. It identified Madison, Wisconsin, as its next planned site for restaurant expansion in the state.

It has been revealed that chipotle Mexican Grill (CMG -2.07%) oversees a chain of restaurants focusing on a limited menu of burritos and bowls made from fresh ingredients. It opened its first restaurant location in Seoul, South Korea on Sept. 2. It appointed Sabir Sami to its Board of Directors on Sept. 14.

Revenue represents the total money brought in by sales before any expenses are deducted. This metric helps investors measure a company's overall size, market footprint, and long-term trajectory..

Sources indicate that CAVA vs. Chipotle Mexican Grill Revenue over the last 8 quarters. Note: for Q1 2025, Q1 2026, the two companies' reporting periods differ in length by more than 14 days due to differing fiscal calendars, which can make the change between quarters look bigger or smaller than an apples-to-apples comparison would show.

It has been revealed that data source: Financial Modeling Prep. Note: for Q1 2025, Q1 2026, the two companies' reporting periods differ in length by more than 14 days due to differing fiscal calendars, which can make the change between quarters look bigger or smaller than an apples-to-apples comparison would show. Data as of Nov. 20, 2026.

It has been revealed that revenue trends between CAVA and Chipotle demonstrate a textbook contrast between an early-stage hyper-growth chain and a mature, massive-scale compounder. While CAVA expanded its trailing 12-month revenue more than three times faster than its restaurant rival, Chipotle generated over nine times CAVA's quarterly sales volume with greater seasonal stability.

CAVA's brisk top-line expansion is heavily fueled by aggressive store count growth. It reached 500 locations in the third quarter of 2026 on its path toward 1,000 stores by 2032. Chipotle's sales expansion also relies on newly introduced store openings, but with over 4,000 locations, it also relies on revenue growth in existing stores.

In a recent development, due to CAVA's rapidly expanding revenue, its share price valuation has soared. Its forward price-to-earnings ratio exceeds 71 while Chipotle is at a far more reasonable 27. As a result, CAVA's share price heavily depends on sales growth. If that slows, its stock will fall.

Chipotle's scale allows it to be more resilient. Even when consumer spending tightens and comparable sales flatten, its annual store expansion and high digital mix, which was 38.8% of Q3 food sales, sustain high-single-digit top-line growth and substantial cash flow.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A prominent former Premier League referee has questioned the selection of officiasl for the fixture between Liverpool and Manchester United at Anfield on Sunday.

Sources indicate that as confirmed via premierleague.com, Sam Barrott will take charge of the match, with Adam Nunn and Lee Betts as his assistants, while Chris Kavanagh is fourth official. John Brooks is on VAR, assisted by Paul Howard.

The upcoming game is the Reds’ sixth home match in the top flight this season, and it’ll be the third to have had the Yorkshire native as the referee.

Upon learning that curious fact, Keith Hackett took to social media to endorse Barrott as a referee but question the decision-making process which has led to him being dispatched to Anfield once again.

The former chief executive of the PGMOL (now Pro Ref) posted on X: ‘A top-class referee, but not a very good appointing procedure by his bosses’.

According to recent reports, want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

It’s a strong show of faith by Pro Ref chief executive Howard Webb to assign Barrott to what is always the most high-profile fixture in English football, and arguably world football.

Liverpool fans might be forgiven for not being able to summon much enthusiasm over the appointment, given the official’s previous at Anfield this season.

Sources indicate that in August, it was he who awarded Nottingham Forest a penalty in their 2-2 draw against the Reds when Neco Williams went to ground under a challenge from Alisson Becker. The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents Panel subsequently adjudged that the spot kick was wrongly given.

While there are clear critera which must be observed when appointing match officials to specific fixtures – any officials from Merseyside or Manchester are obviously ineligible for Sunday’s clash at Anfield – seeing Barrott assigned to yet another Liverpool home game does seem anomalous.

According to recent reports, we just hope – for his sake as much as anyone else’s – that the main talking point after the final whistle isn’t a controversial and decisive error on his part. The last thing we need is yet more dubious refereeeing affecting the Reds.

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (687 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Netflix's (NFLX -2.96%) share price has been cut in half from the all-time high it reached last summer.
  • According to recent reports, while there are reasons for the huge drop in Netflix, including slowing revenue growth and concerns about engagement, the drop prompted billionaire investor Bill Ackman to add the stock back to Pershing Square's (PS -8.77%) portfolio earlier this year.
  • Sources indicate that to be sure, Netflix's revenue growth has slowed considerably this year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adam Levy – Nov 21, 2026 at 11:00PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Netflix ›.

Netflix's (NFLX -2.96%) share price has been cut in half from the all-time high it reached last summer. The stock now trades below $60 per share, as of this writing.

According to recent reports, while there are reasons for the huge drop in Netflix, including slowing revenue growth and concerns about engagement, the drop prompted billionaire investor Bill Ackman to add the stock back to Pershing Square's (PS -8.77%) portfolio earlier this year. The stock has continued to drop, though, but Ackman doesn't see that as a concern. In fact, he sees it as an incredible opportunity for investors.

Sources indicate that to be sure, Netflix's revenue growth has slowed considerably this year. Revenue grew between 15.9% and 17.6% in the four quarters through the first quarter of this year. That rate slowed to 13.4% in the second quarter and 11.8% in the third quarter. Management forecasts just 11.5% growth in the fourth quarter.

Industry observers note that management wasn't afraid to touch on the reasons for the slowdown. Co-CEO Ted Sarandos remarked the U.S. is "just not growing as fast as it could or as fast as we'd like," during the manufacturer's third-quarter earnings call. The advertising business has also been weaker than expected. "We are presently a bit behind our aggressive target for the year," Co-CEO Greg Peters said on the call. And that stems from disappointing engagement. "We want to grow view hours faster. We're not satisfied. We're working on it," CFO Spencer Neumann said.

But investors may be overlooking a key detail about Netflix's business that hasn't changed even as revenue growth slows. Management is highly effective at dialing in content spend and reaching its target operating margin. Operating margin is on track to reach 31.5% this year, up from 29.5% last year.

Sources indicate that what's more, Netflix's free cash flow conversion is very high and growing. It generated $9.5 billion of free cash flow through the first three quarters of the year. Netflix uses that cash to buy back shares, which supports significant improvements in its earnings per share.

In a recent development, that's where Ackman believes the current share price makes Netflix stock a compelling buy. "We'll make more money over time if the stock is cheaper in the short- to intermediate-term because they're going to cancel a lot more shares as a result," he noted in a recent interview.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Industry observers note that netflix repurchased $4.8 billion of its stock in the third quarter, and it still has $22.3 billion in authorization capacity. At the company's current share price, the remaining authorization represents around 9% of the current share count.

Recent findings suggest that netflix could complete the remaining authorization over the next two years. Management expects to generate about $2.5 billion in free cash flow in the fourth quarter, and that number should steadily climb next year. The company should be able to maintain its double-digit revenue growth rate for the foreseeable future with improvements in advertising, pricing, and maintaining a low churn rate while operating margin continues to expand. That should result in higher free cash flow conversion, meaning free cash flow grows even faster than earnings.

Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta Platforms Is Pouring Up to $145 Billion Into AI This Year. Investors Should Watch This 1 Number.

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (750 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that mark Zuckerberg founded Facebook in his Harvard dorm room in 2004.
  • According to recent reports, that sort of value creation should force investors to always give Zuckerberg free rein over his vision and how he directs the organization's financial resources and talent.
  • It's much harder now to believe that Zuckerberg is following the right strategic path.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Neil Patel – Nov 21, 2026 at 11:11PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Meta Platforms ›.

Recent findings suggest that mark Zuckerberg founded Facebook in his Harvard dorm room in 2004. It didn't take long to grow the social media platform into one of the most powerful technology enterprises on Earth. Called Meta Platforms (META -5.93%) today, it sports a market capitalization of $1.6 trillion.

According to recent reports, that sort of value creation should force investors to always give Zuckerberg free rein over his vision and how he directs the organization's financial resources and talent. This is true even though recent blunders, like the metaverse project, haven't panned out. The ”Magnificent Seven” stock is up more than 1,500% since the initial public offering (as of Nov. 17), so his actions have clearly benefited shareholders.

It's much harder now to believe that Zuckerberg is following the right strategic path. Meta will invest up to $145 billion in capital expenditures (capex) in 2026, with spending likely to be much higher next year. This has turned free cash flow negative and led to a pause in share buybacks.

In a recent development, in Zuckerberg's mind, it's all about artificial intelligence (AI). Nervous investors need to watch this one number to judge if all this capex is actually worth it.

It has been revealed that meta's entire business model rests on monetizing the attention of people who interact with its free social media services. It currently has 3.64 billion daily active owners across its family of apps, a gigantic figure that somehow keeps growing. The firm makes its money from advertising, which represented 98% of total revenue in Q3 2026.

In a recent development, the logical conclusion is that Meta's AI-related spending spree is the right move if it improves advertising metrics. So far, this appears to be the case. This is already a huge business, but the growth has been fantastic.

Ad revenue rose 25.9% year over year to $63.1 billion in the third quarter. This is just slightly below what Alphabet's (GOOGL -2.70%) (GOOG -2.59%) Google Search, which is growing at a much slower pace, generated in Q3. Digging deeper, Meta's average price per ad increased 14%, and impressions were up 10%.

The ad ecosystem operates like a flywheel, benefiting from a robust network effect. Improving algorithms drive higher user engagement. Data is collected on their interests. Consequently, this attracts advertisers that want to get in front of these people. Meta generates revenue that is reinvested into its technology stack, further reinforcing the feedback loop.

According to recent reports, AI appears to be strengthening the overall ad ecosystem. On the engagement front, advanced AI models bolster content recommendation. For advertisers, Meta is "leveraging AI to make it easier for businesses to manage campaigns, develop creative, and act on performance opportunities," according to chief financial officer Susan Li.

The organization has developed and rolled out other AI-related offerings. It sells AI tools to small businesses and enterprises. There is insatiable demand for excess compute, which Meta previously noted it can sell at premium prices to outside customers. The popular Muse personal agent can bring in subscription sales and capture commerce revenue share as well. These are immaterial right now, however.

Advertising is the most vital area that investors should watch closely. It's a signal that the hundreds of billions of dollars in capex is driving better financial performance in the core operations. And perhaps most importantly, a thriving ad segment suggests Meta's economic moat is widening.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

The AI infrastructure providers get all the love from Wall Street. This includes the chipmakers, cloud platforms, and AI model developers. Their trillion-dollar valuations reflect the market's appreciation.

But maybe the ultimate winners won't be the companies creating AI. That's an idea worth considering. Most of the value could eventually accrue to businesses that leverage this impressive technology to better serve their customers and improve their lives in unique ways.

Based on how well its ad machine is working, Meta is doing exactly this.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 16, 2026, SharonAI (SHAZ -18.06%) introduced an annualized run rate (ARR) revenue metric to track its commercial expansion as data center infrastructure comes online. Commercial execution now determines whether its contractual backing turns into actual cash flow. Three things management stated on the call stand out.

The tech giant's annualized run rate revenue, or projected yearly revenue based on active billing, will surge as 30 megawatts of data center power capacity enter active service. That operational activation converts initial infrastructure installations into cash-generating deployments under long-term agreements, with billing expected in January of 2027.

Rather than tapping high-cost corporate borrowing, management finances graphics processing unit (GPU) hardware using special purpose vehicles (SPVs), or isolated subsidiary companies created for specific infrastructure projects. These debt facilities lock in funding directly against customer agreements where clients must pay regardless of usage.

Sources indicate that customer pricing on multiyear agreements has increased as specialized compute capacity grows scarce across global markets. High contribution margins, or the proportion of revenue remaining after direct operating costs, allow project returns to pay back initial equipment costs well inside contract terms.

Sources indicate that customers are scrambling for immediate power and compute access, and management is not hiding its satisfaction about its secured data center footprint. The company holds pre-connected power infrastructure in Australia and an anchor partnership with NVIDIA, giving it clear advantages over rivals stuck in utility grid delay queues. Management keeps a close watch on cluster deployment timelines and debt execution.

Converting a total contract value of $9.6 billion into active billing remains the ultimate test for the business as it ramps hardware deployments into 2027.

Where Will Nvidia Stock Be in 20 Years? The Answer Might Surprise You.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) stock is currently the cheapest it has been in over a decade.
  • The manufacturer's shrinking valuation has little to do with its current financial situation.
  • It has been revealed that the macro environment for Nvidia is similarly bullish.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ryan Vanzo – Nov 22, 2026 at 12:00AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

Recent findings suggest that nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) stock is currently the cheapest it has been in over a decade. Shares trade at just 16 times trailing earnings. That's even cheaper than the company's previous decade-low valuation set in early 2019.

The manufacturer's shrinking valuation has little to do with its current financial situation. The GPU maker generated $43.8 billion in free cash flow last quarter. Sales growth this year is expected to approach 100% year over year, with another 71% growth expected the following year. Profits are expected to rise in tandem, causing shares to trade at less than 10 times forward earnings.

It has been revealed that the macro environment for Nvidia is similarly bullish. Research from Apollo Global Management (APO -4.41%) states:.

Recent findings suggest that what, then, is dragging down Nvidia stock? There are three main culprits.

Industry observers note that first, the company is dealing with the ongoing fallout of CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The company could face regulatory blowback, export restrictions, and weaker long-term leadership following Huang's exit.

Second, reporting suggests that Nvidia engaged in a form of circular financing, injecting cash into artificial intelligence (AI) start-ups to absorb excess GPU supply.

Third, investors are concerned about potential margin compression as both hyperscalers and other GPU producers invest aggressively to scale their own chip production.

But here's the thing: If you commit to a 20-year holding period, few of these current concerns will ultimately matter.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

In a recent development, normally, it is difficult to forecast a company's next couple of decades. Nvidia's situation is surprisingly straightforward. While the company's dominant market share in AI GPUs is driven by long-term planning and software ecosystem investment, sales growth is largely driven by industrywide demand. In other words, Nvidia is a high-quality boat in a tide that will rise for decades to come.

"Nvidia has a wide economic moat," asserts research from Morningstar. "[I]ts competitive advantages should allow it to sustain profitability for 20 years," as its products and software are "needed to enable the exponentially growing market around artificial intelligence.".

How swiftly is that AI market growing, and how long will it sustain those growth rates?

It has been revealed that "A massive wave of data center construction will have implications through 2050," stresses research from PwC. "The AI infrastructure cycle underway will likely dwarf previous investment booms in areas like railways, electrification, or the internet.".

In no scenario does PwC forecast data center spending to fall under $20 trillion by 2050.

"Across all three scenarios, capex rises significantly through 2050," the firm predicts. "Faster AI adoption pushes capex to about $50 trillion through 2050; a slower adoption path limits the cycle to roughly $20 trillion.".

While former CEO Jensen Huang was critical in developing Nvidia's current chip lineup and CUDA developer ecosystem, Nvidia's long-term future now relies just as much on industry trends as tech giant-specific development.

Similarly, while near-term regulatory pressure or export restrictions may slightly reduce sales growth, the long-term global growth outlook remains intact.

Sources indicate that margin compression over time, meanwhile, is almost a certainty. But trading at less than 10 times forward earnings, much of these pressures are arguably already priced in. Compounding double-digit annual sales growth -- which should persist over the next two decades -- should more than offset margin normalization, especially considering the next few years should still generate industry-leading profitability.

What will Nvidia be like 20 years from now? The firm will almost certainly be much bigger than it is today. And given how cheaply the stock is priced, I'm fairly certain that patient shareholders will be pleased following a multi-decade holding period.

Robinhood shares fall as crypto slump weighs on profits, offsetting gains in newly introduced businesses

📅 27 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (328 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.
  • Here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept.
  • Robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.

Here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

Robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.

Robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly crucial sources of transaction revenue, while the manufacturer has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.

Transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.

Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.

Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.

Net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

—With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney.

Rashford returns and Fernandes misses another penalty as Man Utd humbled by Amorim

📅 15 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2847 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.
  • Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.
  • His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

Amorim’s Milan equalised after a defensive mix-up allowed Gonçalo Ramos to break into the area and square for Samuel Chukwueze to roll home.

United were awarded their penalty just before half-time after Koni De Winter tugged back Youri Tielemans, but Torriani guessed correctly to leave Fernandes frustrated.

United retook the lead after Patrick Dorgu pounced on a loose backpass from Filippo Terracciano, but Milan equalised again when Chukwueze’s wayward shot was poked in by Alphadjo Cissè at the far post.

Marcus Rashford, who was frozen out by Amorim and loaned out to Aston Villa and then Barcelona, came on as a substitute on the hour for his first United appearance since returning from Spain.

But Milan went ahead in the 68th minute when Chukwueze’s cross was headed home by Ramos, and three minutes later former Chelsea midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek raced through to hit the fourth and cap a performance that underlines United’s need for reinforcements before their season starts in earnest next Saturday, away at Hull City.

Manchester United (4-2-3-1) Lammens; Mazraoui (Dalot 61), Maguire, Heaven (Martinez 61), Shaw; Tielemans, Santos (Mainoo 61); Diallo (Lacey 61), Fernandes, Dorgu (Rashford 61); Cunha (Mbeumo 61). Subs Zirkzee, Yoro, J Fletcher, T Fletcher, Amass, Collyer, Mee (g), Heath (g), Gabriel. Booked Dorgu.

Industry observers note that AC Milan (3-4-2-1) Torriani; Terracciano (Gila 60), Winter (Vladimirov 84), Pavlovic (Diawara 84); Chukwueze, Musah (Ricci 76), Jashari (Modric 60), Estupinan (Bartesaghi 61); Loftus-Cheek (Comotto 84), Cisse (Saelemaekers 60); Ramos (Camarda 75). Subs Pittarella (g), Bouyer (g). Booked Estupinan.

Goals Chukwueze (37), Cisse (57), Ramos (68), Loftus-Cheek (71).

That six-time Champions League winner Luka Modric raised the trophy with the one hand mentioned everything you need to know about this moment...

Aug 22: Hull City vs Manchester United.

Aug 30: Manchester United vs Ipswich Town.

Sep 6: Everton vs Manchester United.

Sep 13: Manchester United vs Manchester City.

Sep 20: Fulham vs Manchester United.

United’s pre-season ends in defeat. A wretched second half proves their undoing as Amorim’s Milan score four. Worth reminding that United led this match, twice.

Milan are playing keep-ball in these latter stages and although Mainoo regains possession, his attempt to play forward is cut out and Modric’s outside-of-the-foot pass finds Comotto, who heads straight at Lammens.

Four minutes of added time to be played...

United now raining crosses down on Milan’s box but Torriani equal to it every time.

For the second time this afternoon, Shaw directs a lovely ball into Fernandes’ path in behind Milan’s back line, but the Portugal international can’t bring it under his spell.

In a recent development, martinez has added a little bit of urgency to United’s build-up. Mbeumo tries to feed Shaw down the line but the ball is cut out.

Sources indicate that more substitutions... Diawara, Vladimirov and Comotto enter the field of play in place of Pavlovic, De Winter and Loftus-Cheek.

Big chance for Rashford! Martinez lofts a fantastic ball over the top but Rashford is not quite able to bring it under his spell, with Torriani and De Winter combing to clear their lines.

Recent findings suggest that milan are now sitting off, settling into a back five as they look to preserve their advantage. Fernandes, Tielemans and Dalot combine well but such has been United’s fortunes this afternoon, the ball ricochets off the referee and play is halted.

Good work from Rashford in the corner to regain possession, but his ball into the box is not picked up by a team-mate.

According to recent reports, more changes... Ramos and Musah make way for Camarda and Ricci.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 4 (Loftus-Cheek) No sooner had the players returned after the second-half hydration break then Milan exploit United’s exposed left side (again). Ramos sends Loftus-Cheek through and the midfielder composes himself before bending the ball around Lammens.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 3 (Ramos) That’s too easy. United fail to learn their lesson, Shaw not getting tight enough to Chukwueze and the winger’s cross is met by fresh signing Ramos, who powers a header back across goal and past Lammens.

Loftus-Cheek and Ramos are doing a good job of cutting off the pass into United’s midfield in their build-up phase.

Wholesale changes on the hour mark...

Rashford (who makes his first United appearance in almost two years), Lacey, Dalot, Mbeumo, Mainoo and Martinez replace Dorgu, Amad, Mazraoui, Cunha, Santos and Heaven.

For Milan, Saelemaekers, Bartesaghi, Gila and Modric are on for Cisse, Estupinan, Terracciano and Jashari.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 2 (Cisse) United have set a higher defensive line so far this half, with their front line pressing with more intensity to avoid the ball over the top. However Chukwueze is able to find space around the sides, coming in off the right and curling an effort goalwards which Cisse turns in at the far post. There are calls for offside, but with no VAR here, the goal stands.

It has been revealed that milan win a free-kick some 25 yards out after Fernandes clips Estupinan. Teenager Cisse steps up and fires straight into the United wall. Was always going to be difficult to trouble Lammens from there.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 1 (Dorgu) United wisely decide to keep hold of the ball for a while, the midfield three rotating to disrupt Milan’s out-of-possession shape and open up passing lanes. A Milan throw-in from the right-back berth is precedes an awful backpass by Terracciano which is pounced on by Dorgu who curls the ball beyond Torriani.

United have looked bright in the opening moments of this half. They win a free-kick midway into Milan’s half. The ball is delivered to the back post and, after some 18-yard-box pinball, a relieved Torriano pounces on it.

Both teams remain unchanged as the second 45 minutes begin.

Recent findings suggest that all square at the break. Tough to know what to make of that half – United looked solid enough and could have taken a lead into the interval had Fernandes converted his penalty, but they failed to create a wealth of clear-cut chances. It will be interesting to see how Carrick approaches this second half.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In the last seven weeks, two low-cost stock funds have moved in opposite directions.
  • It has been revealed that the Vanguard Morningstar Growth ETF (VUG -5.32%) closed Oct.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Daniel Sparks – Nov 22, 2026 at 12:37AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Vanguard Morningstar Growth ETF ›.

In the last seven weeks, two low-cost stock funds have moved in opposite directions.

It has been revealed that the Vanguard Morningstar Growth ETF (VUG -5.32%) closed Oct. 6 at a record $92.64. As of this writing, it trades near $76, about 18% under that high. The Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD -0.76%), meanwhile, is up about 3% since Oct. 6 and is within about 6% of its own record.

Recent findings suggest that that split is a major reason I like owning these two funds together. The growth fund holds many of the fastest-growing large businesses in the U.S., while the dividend fund pays a yield over eight times the growth fund's. And when one has a rough patch, the other has tended to hold up better.

The growth fund tracks the Morningstar US Large Cap Growth Index, and it owned 135 stocks at the end of September. At the time, Nvidia, Apple, Microsoft, and Alphabet accounted for about 45% of the fund's assets.

Sources indicate that technology stocks make up about 69% of the fund by Vanguard's classification. But it's not just a tech fund. Its 10 biggest holdings also include Amazon and Tesla, and consumer discretionary stocks are around 13% of the portfolio.

According to recent reports, what investors get for that concentration is growth. By Vanguard's measure, the fund's current stocks grew their earnings around 33% a year on average in the last five years, and the fund was valued at about 29 times earnings at the end of October. Its share price has dropped about 11% since then, so that valuation arguably looks more reasonable now. In the 10 years through Sept. 30, the fund returned around 18% a year. What's more, its 0.03% expense ratio means just $3 in yearly costs per $10,000 invested.

NYSEMKT · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Sure, that sort of growth can come with bigger drops. The fund lost around 33% in 2022, counting dividends.

According to recent reports, its 30-day SEC yield (a standardized gauge of the income a fund earns) is also just 0.37%. Put another way, dividends don't do much to cushion a fall like the current one.

I wouldn't bet on a quick bounce. But I think 10 years is long enough for companies that have grown this fast to grow into their prices.

Industry observers note that schwab's fund tracks the Dow Jones U.S. Dividend 100 Index, which chooses dividend payers using financial ratios meant to point to the quality and sustainability of their payouts. It owned 102 stocks as of Nov. 19.

Its biggest holdings were Procter & Gamble, Texas Instruments, Coca-Cola, and Home Depot, all between around 4% and 5% of the fund. The mix looks almost nothing like the growth fund's. Consumer staples, healthcare, and energy stocks made up around 55% of the portfolio in Schwab's newest breakdown, but information technology was about 12%.

Industry observers note that income is the top reason to own it. Its 30-day SEC yield was 3.18% as of Nov. 18, and it costs 0.06% a year, or $6 per $10,000.

NYSEMKT · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Schwab, meanwhile, put the fund's holdings at around 18.5 times earnings at the end of October, well under the growth fund's 29 times earnings (but the two companies might calculate the number a bit differently).

This fund won't keep up when growth stocks are running, though. It returned around 12% a year in the decade ending Sept. 30, versus about 18% for the growth fund. Its dividend growth has also cooled. The last four quarterly distributions total around $1.05 a share, only about 2% more than the four before them.

The two funds' best and worst years haven't matched up. In 2022, the growth fund fell around 33% but the dividend fund lost only about 3%, including dividends. The next year flipped that, with the growth fund returning about 47% in 2023 and the dividend fund about 5%. And since Oct. 6 this year, the growth fund has slid around 18% but the dividend fund has risen about 3%.

Someone dividing $10,000 equally between them would pay about $4.50 a year in fund costs and earn a combined yield of around 1.8%.

Over the next decade, I'd expect the growth fund to do most of the heavy lifting on returns, but likely not at its 18% yearly rate of the last decade. The dividend fund's job is to keep cash coming and hold up when growth stocks sell off, the way they have since October.

In a recent development, I'd consider buying both funds today. And with the growth fund around 18% off its record, it's the one I'd add to first.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic underwriters have officially exercised their overallotment of shares in the historic initial public offering, bringing the total raised to $93.5 billion, according to a release Friday.

The artificial intelligence firm raised $81.3 billion on Wednesday and netted an additional $12.2 billion through the overallotment, surpassing SpaceX, which held a record IPO in June.

Industry observers note that anthropic mentioned it sold an aggregate of 1,127,000,000 shares of its Class A common stock at $83 per share in the offering. It sold 980 million shares on Wednesday and its underwriters had the option to purchase up to an additional 147 million shares by Friday as part of the overallotment, which is commonly referred to as the "greenshoe.".

Sources indicate that shares of the Claude maker opened trading at $111.50 on the Nasdaq on Thursday, but slid throughout the day and closed at $97.17. The stock sank 12% in premarket trading on Friday during a broad tech sell-off.

In addition to the sale of its Class A common stock, Anthropic closed a concurrent sale of its Class N common stock after a group of tech companies, including Advanced Micro Devices, Google, Microsoft, Nvidia and others, agreed to participate in a $26 billion private placement at the IPO price. Anthropic mentioned Friday that aggregate gross proceeds from its IPO, including the private placement, totaled $119.5 billion, before deducting offering expenses.

Anthropic dodged an unforgiving series of obstacles on its road to the Nasdaq on Thursday, as investors brooded over Jensen Huang's shocking ouster at Nvidia, voters' stinging rebuke of the tech during the midterms and whether rising interest rates would stymie industry aims for a multitrillion-dollar AI infrastructure buildout.

CEO Dario Amodei co-founded the company in 2021 after he and a handful of other researchers, including his sister Daniela, quit their jobs at OpenAI, now Anthropic's chief rival. Anthropic is best known for developing a family of AI models called Claude, which have captivated the corporate world and fueled the company's historic rise.

The siblings celebrated the IPO as a "milestone" in an interview with CNBC on Thursday, but stated there's more work ahead for Anthropic.

In a recent development, "For us, it's like one stop on the journey," Daniela Amodei mentioned. "We think about this as, 'Wow, this is an incredible moment for Anthropic for our mission, but we're going to wake up tomorrow and we're going to be the same company.'".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lee Samaha – Nov 22, 2026 at 1:07AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Grail ›.

Grail (GRAL -5.33%) stock has been highly volatile in 2026, and that trend looks set to continue next year as well. Management expects its multi-cancer early detection (MCED) test, Galleri, to be approved in the first quarter of 2027, but that's only part of the story. Here's what investors need to know and where the stock could be heading next year.

Sources indicate that the manufacturer finalized its pre-market approval submission for Galleri in late January, only to follow up with disappointing top-line results from its landmark three-year trial of Galleri with England's National Health Service (NHS). The trial failed to meet its primary endpoint of a statistically significant reduction in the diagnosis of late-stage (III and IV) cancers in a population of 142,000.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Recent findings suggest that the principle was that Galleri would detect cancers at an early stage (I and II), leading to less expensive, less intrusive, and more comfortable treatments and, ultimately, better patient outcomes. The trial's overall failure obviously raised concerns about FDA approval and, more importantly, insurer coverage of the test. That's the crash you can see in the stock in February.

While the trial's result was disappointing across the more than 50 cancers it tests for, it did demonstrate more compelling data across the 12 most deadly cancers (including anus, bladder, colorectal, head and neck, lung, ovary, pancreas, and stomach) that cause two-thirds of the deaths in the U.S.

Recent findings suggest that as such, management continued to build the case that the Galleri test data were compelling enough to convince the FDA to approve the test and spur insurer adoption. It's a case that management highlighted at the American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) meeting at the end of May, when outlining both the NHS trial and a smaller 35,000-patient trial in the U.S. and Canada.

The stock then soared in September after an FDA panel voted in favor of Galleri's safety, effectiveness, and benefit, paving the way for FDA marketing approval in 2027.

It has been revealed that the ultimate adoption of Galleri by insurers and medical bodies relies on a somewhat complex set of factors and criteria that don't lend themselves to a binary assessment of trial results. For example, a medical insurer is highly likely to conduct a cost-benefit analysis, weighing the benefits of early detection against the test's cost relative to alternative tests and the cost of false positives.

False positives not only cause significant and unnecessary stress in a patient population, but they also create unnecessary costs, as the positively tested patients will undergo more costly and specific diagnostic testing to determine whether they have cancer with a higher degree of accuracy.

Readers interested in more detail on such matters can read an analysis of the two Galleri trial results in a previous article. Suffice it to say that it isn't simply a matter of the FDA approving the Galleri test and insurers adopting it en masse; the test also needs to demonstrate its commercial viability to insurers.

In addition, management has high hopes that Medicare will reimburse Galleri under the Nancy Sewell ACT, which allows coverage and payment for FDA-approved MCED tests if the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) "determines such coverage is appropriate.".

Management is in contact with the CMS and expects it to initiate a National Coverage Analysis (NCA) following FDA approval (hopefully in early 2027), culminating in a National Coverage Determination (NCD) about a year later.

Industry observers note that therefore, the sequence of events next year is FDA approval, which then opens up more detailed conversations with commercial payers and insurers, and initiation of an NCA by the CMS. Ultimately, the key to Grail and Galleri's future may not be commercial payers' decision to adopt the test; it may come down to the price they are willing to pay for it. Grail's management thinks the Galleri test will ultimately settle in a $500 to $600 range, with Wall Street analysts modeling $574 in 2029.

That would be a favorable outcome for Grail, but there's a long way to go before it takes place, and the first step is FDA approval.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • "I did discuss that with President Xi, and he stated, 'Oh, brilliant, brilliant!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that president Donald Trump on Friday stated he and Chinese leader Xi Jinping discussed their shared affinity for former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang during their talks in China this week. Earlier in the day, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the ousted leader was not mentioned in separate talks he had with Chinese officials.

"I did discuss that with President Xi, and he stated, 'Oh, brilliant, brilliant! He's a brilliant man.' He is," Trump said at a White House press conference.

Asked earlier Friday on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" if Huang, a close ally of Trump's, had come up in "any of your discussions with the Chinese," Bessent noted "no," without elaborating.

A senior Trump administration official later said that both Trump's and Bessent's remarks were correct, and that both were addressing their own conversations. The official spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss those conversations.

Trump also reiterated that he would like to see Huang — who was replaced by interim CEO Colette Kress after resigning amid allegations of an extramarital affair with a Chinese spy — be restored as Nvidia's CEO.

In a recent development, "I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance," Trump remarked. "You know, we're a country of second chances, and I'd love to be able to see him. That's a very important company to us, and he put us in a position where we are literally 10 years advanced over other companies.".

Nvidia's board is not considering bringing Huang back, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC earlier this week.

The president's comments came amid growing scrutiny of advanced U.S. chips, including those made by Nvidia, ending up in China either legally or by being diverted via third countries.

Both Trump's and Bessent's remarks are potentially an indication that the Trump administration may not focus on cracking down on China's efforts to acquire advanced chips.

Bessent suggested that U.S. policy allowing the sale of Nvidia's powerful H200 AI chips to China remains unchanged following the talks in Shenzhen this week.

"We've already agreed that the ... H200s are the threshold level of chips that could be sold to the Chinese, and, you know, that continues as planned," Bessent mentioned.

"I wouldn't anticipate any change in the policy," he added after CNBC's Sara Eisen noted that Nvidia said it had stopped selling H200s to China.

In a recent development, the administration ignoring the subject of Huang's affair with a possible Chinese spy — whose Singapore-based firm Megaspeed has been accused of acting as a cutout for Beijing — contrasts with the importance Trump has placed on beating China in the race to artificial intelligence dominance. It could suggest that despite his support for the U.S. AI industry, Trump is less concerned with addressing China's ongoing efforts to acquire U.S. semiconductors.

In a recent development, trump has also defended Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who has come under fire from multiple directions for reportedly slow-walking export restrictions on Chinese chip sales. "I understand both sides of it," Trump said on Monday when he also said he's like to see Huang back as CEO.

Bessent's appearance on CNBC came after Trump's return from a tour through Asia that saw him meet with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China.

Sources indicate that the meeting was historic as the first time the leaders of the three countries had met without other nations' counterparts. But the trilateral summit appeared to yield few deliverables on any number of the most pressing global complications related to the countries, including the Ukraine and Iran wars or the ongoing AI race.

Bessent told CNBC on Friday that there was a "robust discussion" between Trump and Xi on trade policy and AI.

They "agreed that humans should always be involved in any military decisions that SI makes, and the SI should not be allowed to be autonomous for major military actions," he said, abbreviating the term "super intelligence," Trump's attempted rebrand of AI.

In a CNBC appearance last week, Bessent lamented the "leakage" of U.S.-made AI chips to China and blamed the Commerce Department, led by Lutnick, for slow-walking export controls on suspected Chinese cutouts like Megaspeed.

Multiple Trump administration leaders have long sought to impose export restrictions on Megaspeed, but Commerce "has the pen" and "you will have to ask them about their internal processes," Bessent stated in that interview.

On Friday, however, Bessent was much more tight-lipped.

According to recent reports, asked if there is a dispute between him and Lutnick over how aggressively the U.S. should be pursuing Chinese export controls, Bessent remarked, "I think we're all committed to following President Trump's instructions.".

In a recent development, "I think we are going to see that the ... proper chip restrictions are in place, and the remote access has been curtailed," he added. Commerce recently took steps to close one of China's paths to accessing AI processors.

Correction: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent spoke to CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." A previous version of this story misstated the name of the show.

#50788. Industry News: Warsh wants Fed officials to talk less. Instead, they’re talking more

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1058 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Warsh wants Fed officials to talk less. Instead, they’re talking more

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1058 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, in his first six months as Federal Reserve chairman, Kevin Warsh has diligently avoided signaling where he sees monetary policy and interest rates headed.
  • Fed officials have been rushing to the microphones lately, voicing sometimes conflicting opinions on how the central bank should be handling an inflation bug that the economy can't seem to shake.
  • Industry observers note that most agree that rates should be raised — and soon.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, in his first six months as Federal Reserve chairman, Kevin Warsh has diligently avoided signaling where he sees monetary policy and interest rates headed. His colleagues have been only too happy to fill the void.

Fed officials have been rushing to the microphones lately, voicing sometimes conflicting opinions on how the central bank should be handling an inflation bug that the economy can't seem to shake.

Industry observers note that most agree that rates should be raised — and soon. Some are willing to hike at a measured pace as conditions play out, while others, such as Governor Christopher Waller and St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem, entertain the thought of more aggressive hikes in a shorter period of time.

Largely on the sidelines in the debate is Warsh, who has expressed disdain for that sort of forward guidance and argued that it handcuffs policymakers long before they actually have to make a decision. But that hasn't stopped most of the other 18 officials who sit in on Federal Open Market Committee meetings.

In fact, according to a Bank of America analysis, there has been more so-called Fedspeak in the past two weeks than in any similar period since the start of 2025.

"Warsh's refusal to guide markets might be encouraging the rest of the FOMC to speak more, not less," Bank of America economist Aditya Bhave said in a note Thursday.

"There is always a range of views across the 19 FOMC participants. Typically, the Chair would weigh in, indicating to markets whether the hawks or doves are in ascendence," he added. "Absent this leadership, however, both sides might feel incentivized to speak more often and more forcefully.".

The increasingly vocal debate comes at a critical time for the Fed and has myriad policy implications.

Sources indicate that bhave noted "a deepening divide" on the FOMC. The Fed's decision not to increase its benchmark rate at its October meeting "increasingly looks like a mistake," and as a result "the hawks have been very vocal of late," he wrote. Leading the charge is Waller, who has raised the possibility of hiking by half a percentage point when the committee next meets in December.

Minutes from the October meeting hint at the tension, particularly when it comes to Warsh's refusal to provide guidance.

The summary related that some officials who were looking for a hike in October "could have supported no change in the federal funds rate provided that it was clearly understood by market participants that further tightening was likely" — a statement that points toward the forward guidance that Warsh has insisted the Fed avoid.

The minutes "revealed that some officials favoring a hike would have accepted a hold if the Fed had clearly communicated further tightening," market veteran Ed Yardeni wrote Thursday. "Warsh's communication philosophy may thus be limiting the Fed's flexibility precisely when it needs it most.".

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, who voted against the October pause in favor of a quarter-point hike, tiptoed around the forward guidance issue during a recent public appearance.

It has been revealed that prefacing some observations she made about where she sees policy headed, Hammack noted that, "Those are not promises. Those are not commitments. They're not forward guidance, which is a hot-button topic. But what they are are a conditional set of expectations of where I think the economy can go, based on what I'm seeing.".

Hammack's comments illustrate a needle that Fed officials have been trying to thread: continuing to be transparent about their thinking without appearing locked into a future policy that changing economic conditions could render obsolete.

Speaking Thursday, Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee framed the argument around credibility.

"I am sympathetic to the view that [Warsh] has expressed that let's not be so, in in our language, forward guidance-oriented, saying here is what I think rates are going to be at the next meeting," Goolsbee mentioned, calling such pronouncements "falsely precise.".

However, he swiftly separated forward guidance from transparency.

"I think central banks should be careful about doing anything that undermines credibility," Goolsbee remarked. "That said, I also think that it's pretty important [that] each person who sits around that table explain how they see the world. What do you see in business conditions? You don't want to surprise everybody.".

Taking a slightly different tack, Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson, in a speech Thursday on policy communication, insisted that markets can figure out where policymakers are going without specific guidance so long as they understand how economic developments will influence decisions.

Paulson also defended the variety of voices coming from the Fed.

"But volume is not the same as clarity," she remarked. "The measure is not how much we say. It is whether we are understood." The mixture of voices "guards against any single communication becoming the only one that matters.".

Financial markets have taken the plethora of Fed communications and interpreted it in a fairly hawkish way.

Sources indicate that traders are implying a 100% chance of at least a quarter percentage point hike in December, with a very small probability of a half-point move, according to the CME Group's FedWatch. From there, odds are high for a follow-up increase in January, then perhaps one more before the end of 2027.

While current inflation indicators are running above 3%, compared to the Fed's 2% target, market measures of longer-term inflation have declined.

Recent findings suggest that five-year forward expectations, as indicated through the Treasury market, are at their lowest since April. That suggests investors could be less concerned about inflation over the longer term, even as policymakers warn that current price pressures remain elevated.

Still, a sclerotic communications strategy from the Fed amid volatile economic and geopolitical currents could prove dangerous ahead.

"The result of this back-and-forth is undue rates volatility in already turbulent times," BofA's Bhave stated.

For his part, Warsh has been advocating for a "family fight" atmosphere inside the Fed, arguing that competing viewpoints deserve a full airing as the committee works towards decisions.

Sources indicate that "There are benefits to shaping the market's future expectations. Perhaps this is part of the 'family fight' that Warsh keeps referencing in his pressers," said Tom Graff, chief investment officer at advisory firm Facet. "That family fight seems to be happening out in public.".

Ikeda thinks that the market is underestimating the growth prospects of DDOG's security products. Meanwhile, he cautioned investors about concentration risk related to large customers.

The analyst stated that Vera Rubin is gaining momentum, though details on next year's Rubin Ultra were lighter than expected.

With demand outpacing supply, Moore noted that focus is on closing the gap. In this regard, he highlighted the supply chain deals on substrate, packaging and testing. While the analyst continues to view TSMC 3 nm wafer supply as the biggest challenge, he expects it to ease over time.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

Data center construction costs soar 13% in 2026

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (518 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The demand for large-scale data centers in the U.S.
  • All that resulted in costs rising 13% year-over-year to more than twice the global rate, according to a new report from Turner & Townsend, a global project management company.
  • Recent findings suggest that the report looked at over 500 live or recently completed projects in 62 global markets.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The demand for large-scale data centers in the U.S. this year, driven by the need for computing power for artificial intelligence, grew well beyond the supply of powered land and the labor to build these structures. It also pushed timelines and risk for contractors.

All that resulted in costs rising 13% year-over-year to more than twice the global rate, according to a new report from Turner & Townsend, a global project management company. The gain this year was about three times the last ten-year average.

Recent findings suggest that the report looked at over 500 live or recently completed projects in 62 global markets. It also included a survey of 400 experts in the global data center industry.

While there was some stabilization in cost inflation this year, it was not enough to offset the huge growth in not just demand but speed of construction and delivery.

In a recent development, "More aggressive schedules tie to contractors in particular and subcontractors baking in more risk allowances in their pricing," said Paul Barry, North America data center lead for Turner & Townsend. "So whether that's acceleration allowances, whether that's more overtime and labor attraction allowances, even just higher fees for taking on the risk of delivering at a faster pace than what they would traditionally take on.".

All of those things, combined with the spike in demand and the strain on the supply chain, translate into higher costs, he added.

In a recent development, capital expenditure on global data centers is projected to rise from about $800 billion this year to $1.8 trillion per year in 2050, according to a recent report from PwC. The U.S. is expected to capture almost half of all global investment in AI infrastructure, which includes both data centers and chips.

Recent findings suggest that power is, of course, key to all data centers, and 56% of those surveyed by Turner & Townsend globally mentioned it was a major obstacle to delivery. Just over half said utility connections typically take between one and two years, and almost a third reported timeframes of over two years. Costs for power vary regionally — from $15.01 per watt in Silicon Valley to $10.51 per watt in Dallas, based on a typical 60-megawatt design.As with every type of construction in the U.S., labor continues to be a significant headwind. Just over one quarter of respondents said their contractor capacity, that is, the ability to manage construction backlogs, was sufficient.

Going forward, Barry mentioned he expects costs to moderate somewhat, with cost increases in the 6% to 10% range in the next year. A lot of the major projects have already started or are starting now, so cost risk has been baked into those contracts.

"If this demand continues, then there'll be more continued flow of project starts and so on, but I think we've hit a significant surge in 2026, especially of fresh big major projects that have been procured," said Barry.

#50779. Tech Report: Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City

📅 16 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 30m • 📚 Deep Dive (5990 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City

📅 16 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 30 min read (5990 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~30 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert?
  • According to recent reports, how about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it?
  • So what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the newly introduced signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

According to recent reports, how about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

So what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

Title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

In a recent development, first Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

Ben White to the rescue with an incredible block 🦸📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZK0cNnFz5N.

Industry observers note that another notable incident was Martin Odegaard, not long after he had glossed a fabulous display with a third goal, sprinting 30 yards to spook Gianluigi Donnarumma and make the Italian hurry his clearance. The victory was good, the trophy was nice, but the energy heartened Arteta more than anything.

In a recent development, “They are really good examples,” Arteta noted. “The way the team tracks back is unbelievable, especially when, fitness-wise, we aren’t there yet. We had desire and composure on the ball. When you put your soul and your heart into every action, this is what happens. We want to do it again.

“The desire comes from them thinking: ‘I want to live that moment again. I want to have all the moments again and I want them to be even bigger.’ We know what it is going to take. We have never done it [retain the Premier League] at this football club. We know it will demand something special.”.

It has been revealed that you could flip that and say it will take something special from the chasers. George Graham and Arsène Wenger could never hold on to the biggest prize during their reigns and you must return to Herbert Chapman, in Arsenal’s thriving 1930s, to find the only manager who went back-to-back.

Industry observers note that it can feel premature (and can be foolish) to go out on a limb before the first weekend, but there was just something about them that felt different. Often in the past they have been overtly tentative when playing City, but they came out of their corner this time swinging – and they landed.

Enzo Maresca revealed afterwards that he “really didn’t like” how Arsenal had scored their first goal and that was putting it mildly, as there were 10 passes – broken only by the ball bouncing off Elliott Anderson’s shins – before Myles Lewis-Skelly ushered Calafiori into wreak havoc.

You had to go back to 1968, when City played West Brom, to find the last first-minute goal – City’s Bobby Owen was the scorer that day – and how Calafiori enjoyed it, shaking his fist in delight as Arsenal’s noisy fans reminded everyone of their status.

Riccardo Calafiori gives Arsenal the lead after just 24 seconds 🤯The assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/aU0UsCB1Xs.

Recent findings suggest that here was a rude awakening for Anderson, City’s newly introduced £116m man. He was ever so slightly off the pace and that allowed Lewis-Skelly to slip a beautiful ball in behind the FA Cup winners’ defence and invite Calafiori to do the rest, which he did with assurance.

When Maresca watches back the video, he will see Abdukodir Khusanov sleeping and Phil Foden failing to press, but that should not detract from the quality of Arsenal’s interchanging – and it should also make whoever is hawking Lewis-Skelly around to clubs to think again. Why would he leave this?

It should not have been the case that a goal so soon should have governed how the game progressed, but that is exactly what happened as Arsenal completely dominated. Whenever they lost possession, they recovered it as a matter of urgency. Without Pep Guardiola on the touchline, City were like Samson after Delilah shaved his hair, devoid of all power.

Recent findings suggest that city, in contrast to their opponents, indicated a complete lack of desire and the second goal arrived when Odegaard was allowed time to flip a ball to the back post, where new boy Tzolis was arriving. The Greek headed back into the six-yard area and Kai Havertz did the rest.

Kai Havertz finishes off a well-worked move to double Arsenal's lead 🤩📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tGkxCIBV8F.

Arsenal were criticised – fairly – during their title-winning campaign for being too physical and relying on gamesmanship, but if Havertz and Odegaard can stay fit for a prolonged period, the difference in style will be like night and day.

According to recent reports, throw in Tzolis, who was tricky and dynamic in Cardiff, to the mix and there will be another enhancement. He looks considerably better than Gabriel Martinelli, with more end product, and Bukayo Saka will do more down the right than Noni Madueke, who started here.

Maresca knew, with his team lacking fitness, that it would be difficult to overhaul the deficit once they had gone two goals behind but, really, he was lucky that Arsenal did not administer a genuine hiding which, at one stage, seemed as though they might.

Goal number three arrived just after the interval, again Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis were involved, combining to enable Odegaard to waltz into the area, hoodwinking Donnarumma so he sat down before sliding a contemptuous finish beyond him.

Take a bow, Martin Ødegaard 😮‍💨Arsenal are flying against Man City!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/cMHbIyJ90D.

Had they gone through the gears, there could have been more, but it didn’t matter. What Arsenal indicated was far more significant than a couple of more goals when the game was being disrupted by substitutions. The tackles, the running, energy and commitment – that is what brought Arteta joy.

“I’m extremely happy with the performance, the result and winning the first trophy,” Arteta purred.

You would be brave to say it will be their last.

The league champions kick-off the domestic season with a resounding and stylish victory. In case any Arsenal fan had forgotten that last season ended with them losing a Champions League final on penalties, City fans are on hand to remind them. They have one European Cup to Arsenal’s zero. Away from the tin foil trophies, I’m sure much bottle-related mirth is on the cards, especially now broadcasters and fans are aware of the viral possibilities. Too aware, I would argue.

The pool of players who can improve the Premier League champions and Champions League finalists is a small one, but it is still fair to point out that Arsenal’s summer has not gone smoothly. They pursued Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior without success, and Arteta’s desire to take the team to a “different dimension” has so far gone unfulfilled., certainly in the forward positions.

Sources indicate that arsenal still look strong, but have they passed up a chance to pull away from the rest? Sam Wallace takes a look at their summer so far.

Recent findings suggest that it would have been less stressful for Guardiola to go once he realised the great side of Kevin De Bruyne was nearing its end. Instead he opted to oversee a rebuild that gives his successor a greater chance of immediate success, going close to the title last season in what was effectively year one for a re-emerging City side. Guardiola must have known he was signing Gianluigi Donnarumma, Antoine Semenyo, Marc Guéhi and Rayan Cherki for someone else’s long-term benefit.

The Community Shield returns to Cardiff’s Principality Stadium for the first time since 2006, and a different dynamic is at play between Arsenal and Manchester City.

When the two clubs played at Wembley in this fixture three years ago, it felt like a more significant occasion for Arsenal as they sought to prove that the gap was closing to Pep Guardiola’s champions.

Now it is Arsenal and Mikel Arteta who have a league title behind them, while Enzo Maresca is the manager hoping to build credibility as City turn the page post-Pep Guardiola.

In truth, these two teams will look very different by the time the season gathers pace in autumn. World Cup exertions mean Elliot Anderson, Erling Haaland, Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka will be minimally involved in this game, while transfer aims remain up in the air for both camps.

According to recent reports, city appear bound to lose Rodri, in addition to Bernardo Silva and Tijjani Reijnders in central midfield. Rodri’s sale would expedite a move for Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi, and possibly Enzo Fernandez despite Chelsea’s insistence that the deadline to sign him for £120m has passed.

Industry observers note that arsenal are also open for business, hoping to add a right-sided defender to help them cope with William Saliba’s absence. The £75m purchase of Bruno Guimarães means the champions’ midfield options look formidable, but so far it has been another summer without a level-raising forward signing. Christos Tzolis in and Leandro Trossard out looks canny business, but falls into the category of like for like.

Sources indicate that although Arsenal held their nerve to see off City in the title race, they failed to win in three attempts against their rivals, including a limp defeat in the Carabao Cup final at Wembley. Arsenal also failed to win, or score, against Liverpool in the Premier League last season so their record in the big games is an area for improvement.

The victors this afternoon will claim to have laid a marker down, the losers will write the game off as a warm up exercise.

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (384 w)
📖 Baca

Industry News: Trump vows to stop U.S. companies from building data centers abroad, threatens 'tremendous tax'

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (384 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that president Donald Trump on Friday noted U.S.
  • "We're going to fight very hard for the data centers," Trump remarked at a White House press conference before announcing the new policy — which apparently came as news to his own staff.
  • According to recent reports, "I don't know if that's a breaking story," Trump mentioned.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that president Donald Trump on Friday noted U.S. companies will be banned from building data centers in other countries and will face a "tremendous tax" penalty if they do so.

"We're going to fight very hard for the data centers," Trump remarked at a White House press conference before announcing the new policy — which apparently came as news to his own staff.

According to recent reports, "I don't know if that's a breaking story," Trump mentioned. "I haven't even said that to my people. But I'm telling them now they're here.".

Recent findings suggest that trump's latest push for more data-center construction in the U.S. came despite Americans repeatedly stating — and showing with their votes — that they dislike the structures.

CNBC's All-America Economic Survey found that 64% of registered voters opposed an AI data center within 10 miles of their home, while just 13% of respondents mentioned they would support one.

It has been revealed that if Trump follows through on his threat to clamp down on overseas data center construction, he will have to contend with the fact that numerous U.S. tech giants — including Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle — have already built them in other countries.

International expansion represents a growth opportunity for the top cloud infrastructure providers, which want to serve clients from data centers that are nearby, sometimes to meet regulatory requirements.

Trump noted Friday, however, that if companies want to continue building the centers outside the U.S., "they can, but we're going to put a tremendous tax on them.".

"We have a lot of places that want them badly, and they're great places. They have energy, and they have everything. They're tremendous assets," Trump said.

Representatives at cloud providers Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Oracle did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Trump's remarks came a day after Trump met with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in China for a trilateral summit that appeared to produce few concrete deliverables on an array of pressing global problems.

Xi "congratulated me on how well we're doing" in artificial intelligence, Trump said, using his preferred term "super intelligence," which he said the Chinese president also likes better.

— CNBC's Jordan Novet and Annie Palmer contributed reporting.
